verdicts.strongest_argument: The load-bearing fact is published in two places: the Hanwha Vision Q2 result itself carried an English wire item (RTTNews, 'Hanwha Vision Q2 Operating Income, Sales Rise'), and the $800m+/10-year multi-generation LTA was a globenewswire press release on 2026-05-28 covered by Investing.com, StreetInsider, StockTitan and Insider Monkey the same day. What is genuinely obscure is only the segment detail (KRW 394.6bn, AI-CCTV 59% of network-camera revenue) in the Korean-language Herald piece. Against that, two things blunt the mechanism. First, Hanwha Vision's own press release states it retains control of its proprietary Wisenet SoC, so the AI-mix shift inside its calendar-Q2 network-camera revenue is not straightforwardly Ambarella silicon; the LTA is forward, multi-generation revenue and cannot be a material contributor to a quarter that ended 31-Jul-26. Second, Hanwha's Apr-Jun quarter sits inside the window Ambarella itself had visibility on when it guided $105.0-111.0m on 2026-05-28, so the datapoint is confirmatory of the guide rather than incremental to it. And 'AI mix shift raises content per camera in professional IoT' is not a discovery: it is the stated bull case in every Ambarella release and in the sell-side notes (Needham, Morgan Stanley, Rosenblatt all publish it). A customer read-across of unquantified size against a 14% implied move is small.

prior_publication.what_it_says: English-language wire item reporting Hanwha Vision's Q2 2026 revenue and operating income rising, with security-segment strength on AI cameras.
Announces the $800m+, ten-year-plus multi-generation edge-AI SoC agreement, and notes Hanwha Vision keeps control of its own Wisenet SoC.
Earlier English coverage of Hanwha Vision's record AI-camera-driven results and rising AI share of network-camera sales, establishing the mix-shift trend well before August.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: None supportive on the bullish side: spot is -20.1% over 20 sessions and -31.5% from the 52-week high, so no run-up consistent with the market marking up professional-IoT read-across after 2026-08-06 — AMBA closed $83.79 on 6 Aug and $65.43 now. put_call_open_interest_ratio 2.14 leans the other way. The front-expiry chain is 1 day to expiry with total OI 5,641 and an ATM bid-ask 68.7% of mid, and the 25-delta skew was rejected as implausible (-40.6 vol points), so the option chain cannot be used to say whether upside is being paid for at all — only the OI ratio is readable, and it is mildly negative.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence that Ambarella silicon (not Wisenet) sits in the specific Hanwha AI-CCTV lines whose mix moved 46%->59%, plus a size estimate showing Hanwha is a >10% customer in the July quarter.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is a re-reading of the baseline's own run_up field, and every input to it is wire copy or the public tape. The FT report was carried by Reuters, Yahoo Finance, Investing.com, StreetInsider and StocksToTrade on 2026-07-31; the +7.08% and +16.08% days and the subsequent bleed are on the free stockanalysis.com history the hunter itself cites. The market does not need to be told why its own price spiked and faded. More importantly, the reinterpretation is partly wrong on its own arithmetic: the -5.4%-vs-SMH--6.6% comparison mismatches windows, taking AMBA from its pre-rumour 29-Jul close ($69.19) but SMH from its 7-Aug peak ($582.70). On a matched window, SMH went 504.22 on 29-Jul to 544.39 on 3-Sep, i.e. +8.0%, against AMBA -5.4% — about 13.4 points of relative underperformance measured from the undisturbed pre-rumour base, which is the opposite of 'in line with the sector'. From 17-Aug the stock ran roughly 2x the sector's decline (AMBA -16%, SMH -8.4%), consistent with a high-beta de-rate plus premium decay rather than with the benign reading. The one residual that is real and not stated in the baseline is that ~two-thirds of the -20.07% run-up field is rumour-premium decay, so the field should not be read as 'bad news leaking'. That is a correction to our pipeline's reading, not information the market lacks, and it reaches tonight only through the reaction function (a live bidder cushions a bad print), not through the numbers.

Free public daily price history showing $69.19 on 29-Jul, +7.08% to $74.09, +16.08% to $86.00, a peak of $86.78 on 7-Aug and the slide to $66.00 on 3-Sep.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The baseline itself carries run_up_20d_pct -20.07 and pct_from_52w_high -31.5, so the drawdown this claim reinterprets is already a sealed field. The two rumour days are visible in the tape and the fade is continuous with no gap, i.e. no single unexplained repricing date to point at. Option chain gives no help: 1 day to expiry, 5,641 total OI, ATM spread 68.7% of mid, skew rejected — so there is no readable deal-probability signal in the vol surface, and I explicitly cannot claim the market is or is not pricing residual deal optionality from this chain.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A dated report between 7-Aug and 3-Sep that the NXP process is still live, or a matched-window relative-performance calculation showing AMBA in line with SMH from the pre-rumour close.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Every figure here is in the 10-Q filed 2026-06-02 and the associated release, and the interpretation was supplied publicly by management on the 28-May call, which the finding itself concedes. StockTitan's filing summary published on 2026-06-02 already tied the margin miss to the same line item — 'Gross margin slipped to 58.4%, mainly from higher manufacturing costs and adverse purchase commitments' — and flagged the $25.6m operating cash outflow 'largely due to inventory build'. The bearish inference is also close to self-cancelling: purchase commitments fall when the wafers have already been taken into inventory, and inventory rose 54% in the same quarter, so a 33% sequential decline in open commitments is the arithmetic complement of the build rather than an order cut. Size is small on the company's own numbers: the first-ever adverse-commitment loss is $1.2m against ~$100m quarterly revenue, and total open commitments of $53.9m are about half a quarter of cost of revenue. Management then guided non-GAAP gross margin UP to 59.0-60.5% from 58.4% actual, which is a public statement that they do not expect the commitment problem to widen. Finally the data is as of 30-Apr-26 and tonight's print supersedes it outright.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Retail-facing summary of the same 10-Q, attributing the 58.4% gross margin to higher manufacturing costs and adverse purchase commitments and the $25.6m cash use to the inventory build.
Q1 FY27 release: inventory $80.4m at 30-Apr-26, and Q2 non-GAAP gross margin guided up to 59.0-60.5%.
Company's own Q1 FY27 call script, the public source for management characterising the inventory build as precautionary against a second-half supply shortage.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: put_call_open_interest_ratio 2.14 says positioning already leans to downside, and the reaction history is 5 down prints in 7 (median absolute move 16.8%, last print -21.4%), so a bearish supply/inventory read is agreement with a tape that already punishes this name. There was no discernible move on 2026-06-02 in the price series relative to the following weeks, so nothing in the baseline shows the market repricing on the 10-Q — but nothing shows it repricing the other way either. The chain's 68.7%-of-mid ATM spread and rejected skew mean I cannot claim downside vol is being bid; only the OI ratio is usable.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A Q2 commitment table showing a second consecutive 30%+ cut alongside inventory that stopped rising, which would break the 'the build explains the cut' rebuttal.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The implication the hunter says nobody drew was drawn, in plain English, on a mainstream retail filing-summary site the day the 10-Q hit: StockTitan on 2026-06-02 wrote that Ambarella 'terminated a development project on May 12, 2026 and agreed to refund $4.5 million of a prior $13.5 million customer deposit, with the remaining $9.0 million to be recognized as a reduction of research and development expense in the next quarter', and explicitly noted that the next quarter is the one ending 31-Jul-26. So this is not an XBRL-only fact; it is a published, correctly-interpreted subsequent-events disclosure three months old. Worse for the claim, the timing cuts against it: the termination was 12-May-26, sixteen days BEFORE the 28-May guide. Management set non-GAAP opex of $56.0-59.0m knowing the credit was coming. Either the credit is inside that guide — in which case consensus, which anchors to Ambarella's opex range, already has it and it is fully priced — or it is not, which would require underlying opex of $65-68m (+16-21% sequentially, far outside this company's history) and therefore implies the company plans to treat the $9.0m as a non-GAAP exclusion, in which case it never touches the non-GAAP EPS the stock actually trades on and only shrinks a GAAP loss that was $18.1m last quarter. Both branches defeat 'unpriced EPS beat'. What survives is modest: that no published preview mentions it, and that if it does land in non-GAAP it is ~$0.20 a share against a ~$0.11-0.15 base, which sell-side would immediately back out as one-time.

prior_publication.what_it_says: States the 12-May-26 termination, the $4.5m refund and that the remaining $9.0m will be recognized as a reduction of R&D expense in the next quarter (the one ending 31-Jul-26).
The 10-Q subsequent-events disclosure itself: $13,500k development deposit liability, $4,500k refund to customer, $9,000k reduction of research and development expense at 31-Jul-26.
Q2 FY27 guide of non-GAAP opex $56.0-59.0m against ~$56.1m Q1 actual, issued sixteen days after the project termination.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: No move around 2026-06-02 distinguishable from the drift (the series traded in the high-$60s through July before the rumour), so nothing in the baseline shows the market marking up a $9m credit — that supports the hunter. Against it, spot is down 20% into the print and put/call OI is 2.14, i.e. positioning is not leaning toward a large opex-driven beat. The 1-day front expiry with 5,641 OI and a 68.7%-of-mid ATM spread means the 14.44% implied move is indicative only and cannot be decomposed into an upside-surprise expectation.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Confirmation from the company or a sell-side model that the $9.0m is included in non-GAAP opex but was NOT in the $56-59m guide, which would make tonight's non-GAAP opex print near $47-50m as a genuine surprise.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is the price itself. 'The premium is gone and nothing was announced' is a statement about the closing print, observable by anyone on the free tape the sibling finding cites, and the underlying deal report was Reuters/FT wire copy on 2026-07-31 that itself said the talks could collapse. The attribution step is also weaker than stated: the finding calls ~13 points 'unattributed to any dated company news' while measuring from 5-Aug ($81.85), a level that only existed because of the 31-Jul FT report — so a large part of that residual IS dated company news, namely the decay of that report. Separately, from 17-Aug to 3-Sep AMBA fell 16% against SMH -8.4% (594.07 to 544.39), roughly 2x beta on a sector drawdown, which explains much of the rest without any hidden company event. I searched for a dated explanation of the 17-Aug-to-3-Sep slide and found none — no downgrade (Needham raised to $100, Morgan Stanley to $96, Rosenblatt reiterated Buy $120 on 31-Aug), no company release, no report the process ended — so the honest reading is beta plus premium decay plus a pre-print de-rate on a name that has fallen on five of its last seven prints, not information leakage. Unexplained relative weakness into a print on a heavily-covered small cap is the most public observation available and put/call OI of 2.14 shows the option market already leaning the same way.

Public daily closes confirming the round trip through the pre-rumour $69.19 to $66.00, i.e. the erased premium is simply the visible price.
SMH closes showing 594.07 on 17-Aug to 544.39 on 3-Sep, the sector drawdown that accounts for roughly half of AMBA's late-August decline at ~2x beta.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: run_up_20d_pct -20.07 and pct_from_52w_high -31.5 are already sealed fields, so the drawdown is in the baseline by construction; realised 20-day vol of 41.3% annualised is consistent with a high-beta unwind rather than an event. put_call_open_interest_ratio 2.14 is the only readable positioning signal and it agrees with the bearish read, which makes this claim confirmation rather than information. The 25-delta skew is null (rejected at -40.64 vol points) and the front-expiry ATM spread is 68.7% of mid on 5,641 contracts of total OI, so I cannot conclude anything from the vol surface about whether downside is being paid for.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A dated, company-specific event in the 17-Aug-to-3-Sep window (order cut, customer loss, confirmed collapse of the NXP process) that would make the residual leakage rather than beta plus premium decay.

interactions: One dominant source cluster and one shared document. CLUSTER 1 — the price series and the NXP rumour: AMBA-a#1 and AMBA-b#2 are the same fact read oppositely. Both rest on the identical stockanalysis.com daily closes and the identical 2026-07-31 FT/Reuters report, both compute essentially the same ~13-point idiosyncratic residual, and both correctly note no report that the talks ended. a#1 reads it as benign premium decay (bullish/neutral, deal option still free); b#2 reads it as unexplained idiosyncratic weakness (bearish). They cannot both add information and should be collapsed to a single residual. On matched windows a#1's specific 'in line with the sector' arithmetic fails — SMH is +8.0% from AMBA's pre-rumour 29-Jul close while AMBA is -5.4%, so the relative de-rate a#1 denies is the same ~13 points b#2 asserts; b#2's magnitude survives but its attribution ('no dated company news') does not, because the base it measures from was created by dated company news. Net: the cluster's largest residual is small and mostly reflects sector beta. CLUSTER 2 — the 2026-06-02 10-Q for the quarter ended 30-Apr-26: AMBA-b#0 (R72, purchase commitments and adverse-commitment loss) and AMBA-b#1 (R76, development deposit) are two footnotes of the same filing, both summarised the same day by StockTitan, so their publication status is identical and they should not be treated as two independent discoveries of unnoticed disclosure. They also point in opposite P&L directions within one quarter (b#0 margin-negative, b#1 opex-positive by $9.0m), and b#1's own timing argument undermines b#0's: management set both the gross-margin guide (up to 59.0-60.5%) and the opex guide with full knowledge of both items. Finally, AMBA-a#0 partially conflicts with AMBA-b#0: a record Hanwha AI-camera quarter is hard to square with a customer-order-cut reading of the 33% commitment decline, which supports the alternative explanation that the commitment fall is simply the complement of the inventory build.
